Let $a,\rho_0>0$, $p_\infty\in\mathbb R$, $U\in\mathbb R^3$, and on $\Omega_a=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:r=|x|>a\}$ define $n=x/r$, $\phi(x)=(U\cdot x)(1+a^3/(2r^3))$, $u=\nabla\phi$, and $p=p_\infty+\rho_0(|U|^2-|u|^2)/2$. Then $u,p$ are smooth in the exterior and up to $r=a$, $u\to U$ and $p\to p_\infty$ uniformly in direction at infinity, and $u\cdot n=0$ on $r=a$. The pair solves $(u\cdot\nabla)u+\rho_0^{-1}\nabla p=0$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, the steady formal constant-density incompressible Euler system. Its boundary condition is impermeable slip/no-through: $u$ is generally nonzero tangent to the sphere, so this is not a no-slip solution. For the formal Euler stress $\sigma_E=-pI_3$ and sphere normal $n=x/a$ pointing from the center into the exterior, the exact resultant is

$$\int_{|x|=a}\sigma_E n\,dS=-\int_{|x|=a}p n\,dS=0.$$

The theorem concerns only this explicit inviscid mathematical model; it asserts neither a viscous zero-drag result nor an observed force. Under SI interpretation, $a,r,x$ are in metres, $U,u$ in metres per second, $\rho_0$ in kilograms per cubic metre, and $p,p_\infty$ in pascals.

proof_steps.text: For $r>0$, $\partial_i(1/r)=-x_i/r^3$ and $\partial_i^2(1/r)=-1/r^3+3x_i^2/r^5$ for $i=1,2,3$, so $\Delta(1/r)=-3/r^3+3r^2/r^5=0$. Since $(U\cdot x)/r^3=-U\cdot\nabla(1/r)$, commuting smooth derivatives gives $\Delta((U\cdot x)/r^3)=0$. Also $\Delta(U\cdot x)=0$, so $\Delta\phi=0$. Therefore $\operatorname{div}u=\Delta\phi=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}u=0$ by equality of the mixed second partials of $\phi$. Direct differentiation yields $u=U+\frac{a^3}{2r^3}\bigl(U-3(U\cdot n)n\bigr)$. This gives uniform $u\to U$ at infinity. At $r=a$, $u=(3/2)(U-(U\cdot n)n)$, which is tangent to the sphere and has zero normal component. [given, F1, algebra]

Let $\chi\in C^2(I\times B;\mathbb R^3)$ be a material motion whose maps $\chi_t$ are orientation-preserving $C^2$ diffeomorphisms onto their open images, and define the Eulerian velocity by $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$. Set $\Omega_t:=\chi_t(B)$ and $\mathcal O:=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\Omega_t\}$. Assume that $\partial_tu$ and all spatial derivatives of $u$ through order two are continuous on $\mathcal O$, that $p$ and its spatial first derivatives are continuous on $\mathcal O$, and that $b\in C^0(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^3)$; here $u$ is in metres per second, $p$ in pascals, and body acceleration $b$ in metres per second squared. In the selected constant-density incompressible Newtonian branch, let the current density be the constant $\rho>0$ kilograms per cubic metre, let $\operatorname{div}u=0$, let the coefficient $\mu$ of the adopted Newtonian closure be constant and denote its value by $\eta>0$ pascal-seconds. Put

$$D(u):=\frac{\nabla u+(\nabla u)^{\mathsf T}}2,\qquad \sigma:=-pI_3+2\eta D(u),\qquad (\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i:=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}.$$

Assume the adopted material linear-momentum balance holds for every nonempty bounded open $V\Subset B$ with $C^1$ boundary, meaning that near each boundary point, after a rigid coordinate change, the boundary is the graph of a $C^1$ function and $V$ lies on one side:

$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho u\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho b\,dx+\int_{\partial\chi_t(V)}\sigma n\,dS,$$

where $n$ is the outward normal and $dx,dS$ are Euclidean volume and area measures. Then throughout each $\Omega_t$ the corresponding local equation is

$$\rho\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)=\operatorname{div}\sigma+\rho b.$$

This is a conditional local form of the adopted balance for the stated smooth material motion and model branch; it makes no existence or empirical-applicability claim.

proof_steps.text: Fix an admissible reference region $V$ and a time $t_0\in I$, and put $K=\overline V$. Its $C^1$ boundary makes $K$ a compact Jordan set. Apply the material-transport identity in [F5], componentwise to $q=\rho u$, on a relatively compact neighborhood of $K$ and a time-translated interval containing $0$ at $t_0$. Because $\rho$ is constant and $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $D_t(\rho u)+(\rho u)\operatorname{div}u=\rho(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u)$. The open-region integral compatibility in [F5] identifies the resulting compact-Jordan integrals with those over $\chi_t(V)$, so $\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho u\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u)\,dx$ at $t=t_0$. [given, F1, F5, algebra]

Apply the material-transport identity in [F5], componentwise to $q=\rho u$, on a relatively compact neighborhood of $K$ and a time-translated interval containing $0$ at $t_0$. Because $\rho$ is constant and $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $D_t(\rho u)+(\rho u)\operatorname{div}u=\rho(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u)$. The open-region integral compatibility in [F5] identifies the resulting compact-Jordan integrals with those over $\chi_t(V)$, so $\frac{d}{dt}\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho u\,dx=\int_{\chi_t(V)}\rho(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u)\,dx$ at $t=t_0$.

proof_steps.text: By [F5], the image $\chi_t(V)$ is a bounded $C^1$ domain. The adopted Newtonian stress [F3] is $C^1$ up to its boundary by the stated field regularity, since $\overline{\chi_t(V)}$ is compactly contained in $\Omega_t$. Apply [F4] to each row of $\sigma$ to replace its traction resultant by $\int_{\chi_t(V)}\operatorname{div}\sigma\,dx$. Substitution of step 1.1 into [A1] gives $\int_{\chi_t(V)}R(t,x)\,dx=0$ for every such $V$, where $R:=\rho(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u)-\rho b-\operatorname{div}\sigma$ is continuous. The hypotheses of [F4] hold by the stated regularity, the $C^2$ motion and [A2]. [given, A1, F3, F4, F5, A2, step 1.1]

The adopted Newtonian stress [F3] is $C^1$ up to its boundary by the stated field regularity, since $\overline{\chi_t(V)}$ is compactly contained in $\Omega_t$. Apply [F4] to each row of $\sigma$ to replace its traction resultant by $\int_{\chi_t(V)}\operatorname{div}\sigma\,dx$. Substitution of step 1.1 into [A1] gives $\int_{\chi_t(V)}R(t,x)\,dx=0$ for every such $V$, where $R:=\rho(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u)-\rho b-\operatorname{div}\sigma$ is continuous. The hypotheses of [F4] hold by the stated regularity, the $C^2$ motion and [A2].

proof_steps.text: Fix $t$ and $x_0\in\Omega_t$. For all sufficiently small $r>0$, the closed ball $\overline{B_r(x_0)}$ lies in $\Omega_t$. Apply [F5]'s $C^1$-image clause to the inverse diffeomorphism $\chi_t^{-1}$ on a neighborhood of this closed ball; then $V:=\chi_t^{-1}(B_r(x_0))$ is bounded, has $C^1$ boundary, and satisfies $\overline V\Subset B$. Step 2.1 gives $\int_{B_r(x_0)}R(t,x)\,dx=0$. If any component $R_i(t,x_0)$ were positive, continuity would make it positive on some sufficiently small ball and force its integral to be positive; if negative, the integral would be negative. Both contradict the zero integral, so $R_i(t,x_0)=0$ for each component. Thus $R=0$ throughout $\Omega_t$, which is the claimed local momentum equation. [given, F5, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
proof_steps.claim: Fix $t$ and $x_0\in\Omega_t$. For all sufficiently small $r>0$, the closed ball $\overline{B_r(x_0)}$ lies in $\Omega_t$. Apply [F5]'s $C^1$-image clause to the inverse diffeomorphism $\chi_t^{-1}$ on a neighborhood of this closed ball; then $V:=\chi_t^{-1}(B_r(x_0))$ is bounded, has $C^1$ boundary, and satisfies $\overline V\Subset B$. Step 2.1 gives $\int_{B_r(x_0)}R(t,x)\,dx=0$. If any component $R_i(t,x_0)$ were positive, continuity would make it positive on some sufficiently small ball and force its integral to be positive; if negative, the integral would be negative. Both contradict the zero integral, so $R_i(t,x_0)=0$ for each component. Thus $R=0$ throughout $\Omega_t$, which is the claimed local momentum equation.

public_sections.Postulate:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the normalized periodic torus convention. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval, let $L>0$ m, and let $\mathbb T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$ have volume measure $dx$ on a period cell and normalized measure $d\mu_L=L^{-3}dx$. Coordinates $x,r,L,\ell$ are measured in metres and time $t$ in seconds. All spacetime fields below use the ordered domain $\mathbb T_L^3\times I$ and evaluation $(x,t)$; for a time-indexed spatial field $q$, write $q(x,t):=(q(t))(x)$. Let $K:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be smooth, dimensionless, supported in a compact subset of $B_1(0)$, and satisfy $\int_{\mathbb R^3}K(s)\,ds=1$. For $0<\ell<L/2$, define

$$G_\ell(r)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}\ell^{-3}K\!\left(\frac{r+Ln}{\ell}\right),\qquad \overline q_\ell(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}G_\ell(r)q(x-r,t)\,dx.$$

The kernel $G_\ell$ has units m$^{-3}$ and filtering preserves the units of $q$.

The physical base model is the smooth, unforced, constant-density incompressible Newtonian branch: $\rho_0>0$ kg m$^{-3}$ and dynamic viscosity $\mu\ge0$ Pa s are constant, $u\in C^1(I;C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^3))$ is periodic with $\nabla\cdot u=0$ and velocity units m s$^{-1}$, and the pressure multiplier is a periodic scalar field $p_{\rm dyn}\in C^1(\mathbb T_L^3\times I;\mathbb R)$ in Pa. Let $I_3$ be the $3\times3$ identity matrix and set $D(u)=(\nabla u+(\nabla u)^T)/2$; the dynamic Cauchy stress is $\sigma=-p_{\rm dyn}I_3+2\mu D(u)$, and $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$ m$^2$ s$^{-1}$. The pressure per unit mass in the filtered equation is the scalar field $\pi=p_{\rm dyn}/\rho_0\in C^1(\mathbb T_L^3\times I;\mathbb R)$ in m$^2$ s$^{-2}$, and $\nabla\pi$ denotes its spatial gradient.

For the filtered velocity $\overline u_\ell$, define its rate-of-strain tensor by

$$D_\ell=\frac12\left(\nabla\overline u_\ell+(\nabla\overline u_\ell)^T\right),\qquad (\nabla\overline u_\ell)_{ij}=\partial_j\overline u_{\ell,i}.$$

The matrix $D_\ell$ has units s$^{-1}$. Use the Frobenius contraction $A:B=\sum_{i,j=1}^3A_{ij}B_{ij}$ for real $3\times3$ matrices.

Adopt the following large-eddy simulation (LES) stress-form closure. A closure here means a specified modeled stress substituted for the exact filtered covariance in the resolved momentum equation. Let $k,\nu_t\in C^1(\mathbb T_L^3\times I;[0,\infty))$ be prescribed model fields, where $k$ represents specific unresolved kinetic energy in m$^2$ s$^{-2}$ and $\nu_t$ is kinematic eddy viscosity in m$^2$ s$^{-1}$. The modeled specific subfilter stress and its modeled transfer are

$$\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}=\frac{2k}{3}I_3-2\nu_tD_\ell,\qquad \Pi_{\ell}^{\rm model}=-\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}:\nabla\overline u_\ell.$$

The closed filtered momentum equation uses the sign convention

$$\partial_t\overline u_\ell+\nabla\cdot(\overline u_\ell\otimes\overline u_\ell)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta\overline u_\ell-\nabla\cdot\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model},\qquad \nabla\cdot\overline u_\ell=0.$$

Both terms in $\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}$ have units m$^2$ s$^{-2}$, and $\Pi_{\ell}^{\rm model}$ has units m$^2$ s$^{-3}$. This is an adopted constitutive form, not a derivation of a physical law: $k$ and $\nu_t$ must be supplied as model inputs or by separate model equations. The prescription does not assert that $\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}$ equals the exact covariance $\overline{u\otimes u}_\ell-\overline u_\ell\otimes\overline u_\ell$, that the modeled tensor is positive semidefinite, or that the closure is empirically adequate in every flow regime. No absence of backscatter for the exact filtered stress is asserted.

public_sections.Statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the normalized periodic torus convention. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval, $L>0$ m, $0<\ell<L/2$, and $\mathbb T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$. Spatial coordinates are in metres and time is in seconds. All spacetime fields below use the ordered domain $\mathbb T_L^3\times I$ and evaluation $(x,t)$; for a time-indexed spatial field $q$, write $q(x,t):=(q(t))(x)$. Let $K:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be smooth, dimensionless, supported in a compact subset of $B_1(0)$, and satisfy $\int K(s)\,ds=1$. Define $G_\ell(r)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}\ell^{-3}K((r+Ln)/\ell)$ and $\overline u_\ell(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}G_\ell(r)u(x-r,t)\,dx$, using volume measure on a period cell. Let $u\in C^1(I;C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^3))$ be periodic and divergence-free, with constant density $\rho_0>0$ kg m$^{-3}$ and constant dynamic viscosity $\mu\ge0$ Pa s. Put $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$ m$^2$ s$^{-1}$ and let $\pi=p_{\rm dyn}/\rho_0$ be pressure per unit mass in m$^2$ s$^{-2}$. Assume the unforced incompressible Newtonian equation

$$\partial_tu+\nabla\cdot(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0.$$

For this filter define the exact covariance stress and transfer by $\tau_\ell=\overline{u\otimes u}_\ell-\overline u_\ell\otimes\overline u_\ell$ and $\Pi_\ell=-\tau_\ell:\nabla\overline u_\ell$. For real $3\times3$ matrices set $A:B=\sum_{i,j=1}^3A_{ij}B_{ij}$ and $|A|_F^2=\sum_{i,j=1}^3|A_{ij}|^2$.

Use the positive smooth unit-mass periodic convolution filter of width $\ell$ to define $\overline u_\ell$. Define the resolved rate-of-strain matrix by

$$D_\ell=\frac12\left(\nabla\overline u_\ell+(\nabla\overline u_\ell)^T\right),\qquad (\nabla\overline u_\ell)_{ij}=\partial_j\overline u_{\ell,i}.$$

The matrix $D_\ell$ has units s$^{-1}$; let $I_3$ be the $3\times3$ identity matrix.

Let $k,\nu_t\in C^1(\mathbb T_L^3\times I;[0,\infty))$ be prescribed specific unresolved kinetic energy and kinematic eddy-viscosity fields, with units m$^2$ s$^{-2}$ and m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, respectively. Adopt the modeled specific stress $\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}=2kI_3/3-2\nu_tD_\ell$ as the replacement for the exact filtered covariance in the resolved model equation, and define $\Pi_{\ell}^{\rm model}=-\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}:\nabla\overline u_\ell$. Then, at every $(x,t)\in\mathbb T_L^3\times I$,

$$\Pi_{\ell}^{\rm model}(x,t)=2\nu_t(x,t)|D_\ell(x,t)|_F^2\ge0,\qquad \tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}:\nabla\overline u_\ell=-2\nu_t|D_\ell|_F^2\le0.$$

If additionally $\nu>0$ and the specific pressure $\pi$ is smooth, the exact filtered-covariance energy theorem applies to this smooth solution. Its resolved-energy balance contains the exact stress contraction $+\tau_\ell:\nabla\overline u_\ell$ on the right-hand side. Replacing that stress slot by $\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}$ in the adopted closure model therefore contributes the displayed nonpositive term to the modeled balance. This is a conditional model deduction; it does not identify the modeled stress with the exact covariance or assert a sign for exact filtered transfer.

public_sections.Statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice for the normalized periodic torus convention. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval, $L>0$ m, $0<\ell<L/2$, and $\mathbb T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$. Spatial coordinates are in metres and time is in seconds. All spacetime fields below use the ordered domain $\mathbb T_L^3\times I$ and evaluation $(x,t)$; for a time-indexed spatial field $q$, write $q(x,t):=(q(t))(x)$. Let $K:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be smooth, dimensionless, supported in a compact subset of $B_1(0)$, and satisfy $\int K(s)\,ds=1$. Define $G_\ell(r)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z^3}\ell^{-3}K((r+Ln)/\ell)$ and $\overline u_\ell(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb T_L^3}G_\ell(r)u(x-r,t)\,dr$, using volume measure on a period cell. Let $u\in C^1(I;C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^3;\mathbb R^3))$ be periodic and divergence-free, with constant density $\rho_0>0$ kg m$^{-3}$ and constant dynamic viscosity $\mu\ge0$ Pa s. Put $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$ m$^2$ s$^{-1}$ and let $\pi=p_{\rm dyn}/\rho_0$ be pressure per unit mass in m$^2$ s$^{-2}$. Assume the unforced incompressible Newtonian equation

$$\partial_tu+\nabla\cdot(u\otimes u)+\nabla\pi=\nu\Delta u,\qquad \nabla\cdot u=0.$$

For this filter define the exact covariance stress and transfer by $\tau_\ell=\overline{u\otimes u}_\ell-\overline u_\ell\otimes\overline u_\ell$ and $\Pi_\ell=-\tau_\ell:\nabla\overline u_\ell$. For real $3\times3$ matrices set $A:B=\sum_{i,j=1}^3A_{ij}B_{ij}$ and $|A|_F^2=\sum_{i,j=1}^3|A_{ij}|^2$.

Use the positive smooth unit-mass periodic convolution filter of width $\ell$ to define $\overline u_\ell$. Define the resolved rate-of-strain matrix by

$$D_\ell=\frac12\left(\nabla\overline u_\ell+(\nabla\overline u_\ell)^T\right),\qquad (\nabla\overline u_\ell)_{ij}=\partial_j\overline u_{\ell,i}.$$

The matrix $D_\ell$ has units s$^{-1}$; let $I_3$ be the $3\times3$ identity matrix.

Let $k,\nu_t\in C^1(\mathbb T_L^3\times I;[0,\infty))$ be prescribed specific unresolved kinetic energy and kinematic eddy-viscosity fields, with units m$^2$ s$^{-2}$ and m$^2$ s$^{-1}$, respectively. Adopt the modeled specific stress $\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}=2kI_3/3-2\nu_tD_\ell$ as the replacement for the exact filtered covariance in the resolved model equation, and define $\Pi_{\ell}^{\rm model}=-\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}:\nabla\overline u_\ell$. Then, at every $(x,t)\in\mathbb T_L^3\times I$,

$$\Pi_{\ell}^{\rm model}(x,t)=2\nu_t(x,t)|D_\ell(x,t)|_F^2\ge0,\qquad \tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}:\nabla\overline u_\ell=-2\nu_t|D_\ell|_F^2\le0.$$

If additionally $\nu>0$ and the specific pressure $\pi$ is smooth, the exact filtered-covariance energy theorem applies to this smooth solution. Its resolved-energy balance contains the exact stress contraction $+\tau_\ell:\nabla\overline u_\ell$ on the right-hand side. Replacing that stress slot by $\tau_{\ell}^{\rm model}$ in the adopted closure model therefore contributes the displayed nonpositive term to the modeled balance. This is a conditional model deduction; it does not identify the modeled stress with the exact covariance or assert a sign for exact filtered transfer.

where $dx$ is volume measure on a period cell. Thus $\overline u_\ell:\mathbb T_L^3\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ is the resolved velocity field, with position in metres and velocity in m s$^{-1}$.
